bib.title: CodeBLEU: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Code Synthesis

question: Can a BLEU variant that adds keyword weighting, AST matching and data-flow matching track programmer judgements of code quality better than BLEU or exact-match accuracy?
hypothesis: Injecting syntax (AST) and semantics (data-flow) into n-gram matching correlates better with human scores than BLEU or perfect accuracy.
contributions: CodeBLEU: weighted combination of BLEU, keyword-weighted n-gram match, AST sub-tree match and data-flow match
Correlation study with programmer scores on text-to-code, code translation and code refinement
Ablation of components and sweep of the four weights

method.summary: Defines CodeBLEU = alpha*BLEU + beta*BLEUweight + gamma*Matchast + delta*Matchdf. Evaluates by Pearson correlation between metric scores and programmer ratings of 3-4 existing systems per task.
method.task: automatic evaluation metric for code synthesis

datasets.name: Text-to-code (Iyer et al. 2018)
datasets.split: 500 random test samples scored; 50 of them human-rated

datasets.name: Code translation Java to C# (Lucene, POI, JGit, Antlr)
datasets.split: 0.5k dev, 1k test; 500 random test samples scored, 50 human-rated
datasets.source: crawled by the authors, paired by file and method name; to be released

models.name: Code translation: PBSMT, Transformer, Transformer+CodeBERT, Human

inference.samples: 500 random test samples per task; 50 human-rated; 20 blocks of 25 for variance

parameters.keyword weight: 5x other tokens in text; Example 1 says 4x (inconsistent)
parameters.weighted n-gram order: keywords considered only in unigrams, N=1, wn=1

metrics.name: Pearson correlation with human score
metrics.definition: correlation between metric and mean programmer rating over the systems of a task

eval.protocol: 10 judges familiar with Java and C#; 50 samples x 4 outputs = 200 pairs, random order, same order for all; paired t-statistic on 20 blocks of 25 sentences

availability.data: code translation dataset promised with scripts

limits: Each correlation is over only 3 or 4 systems and 50 rated samples, so r values are system-level and coarse
No significance test on the correlations themselves
Nothing is executed, so semantic correctness is approximated by data-flow
Accuracy beats CodeBLEU on code refinement (0.999 vs 0.979)
Weights tuned on the same human scores, no held-out check; keyword lists predefined per language and weight 5x vs 4x is inconsistent
Java and C# only; the paper never compares with execution-based metrics beyond describing them

terms.definition: weighted combination of BLEU, weighted n-gram match, syntactic AST match and semantic data-flow match
